info.title: MemeScope AI
info.description: AI-powered Solana meme coin discovery platform. This is the Day 1 platform foundation: auth, health, and plumbing.

get.description:
Report what each pipeline stage has actually produced.

Returns 503 when `overall` is `down`, so this endpoint can drive an
external monitor without that monitor having to parse the body. A
`degraded` roll-up still returns 200: it is a warning, and paging on it
would train the reader to ignore the page.

get.description:
Tokens ranked by their current AI score, filtered and sorted in the database.

Vetoed tokens are excluded unless `include_vetoed` is set: a veto means the risk gate capped the score outright, and such tokens do not belong in a ranking of opportunities by default.

`applied_filters` echoes what was actually applied and `candidate_total` reports the unfiltered population, so an empty page caused by a strict filter is distinguishable from an empty table.

**Pagination note.** Pages are offset-based over a ranking that changes as tokens are re-scored, so a row may shift between pages while a client is walking them. Ordering is total (the sort column plus `mint_address`), so results are deterministic for any single request.

get.description:
The weight vector and thresholds currently in use, including components that are declared but whose data source does not exist yet.

These weights are priors, not fitted parameters. Publishing them is what makes that claim checkable. `available_weight_total` is the ceiling on coverage, and therefore on evidence, for every token scored by this model - which is why `elite_gate.reachable` can be false.

get.summary: Current AI score for a token
get.description:
The token's current score with its full component breakdown and explanation.

A token that exists but has no score returns 200 with `score: null` and a `status` explaining why - the absence is meaningful state, not an error. A mint that was never discovered returns 404.

`confidence` and `freshness` are computed per request from the age of the underlying snapshot, so this response is never stale even when the stored row is.

get.summary: Score history for a token, newest first
get.description:
Recorded score changes for one token.

History is written on material change plus a periodic heartbeat, so this is a record of events rather than a sample of every evaluation. The table is append-only, so offset pagination is stable here.

Weights, gates and categories, verbatim.

Published so the platform's claims about its own model are checkable rather
than asserted — the same reason `/scores/model` exists. `reachable: false`
marks a category the current model can never award.

Aggregate performance across every opportunity ever detected.

Includes failures. A success rate computed only over the entries that
worked is not a success rate, and hiding the losers would make the whole
record worthless as evidence.

get.description:
Opportunities currently on the Radar.

Filters are echoed so an empty page caused by a strict filter is
distinguishable from an empty Radar — the same convention `/scores/top`
follows.

List the configured Pump.fun age and market window.

This route is intentionally separate from ``GET /radar``: an admission
candidate has not passed the Opportunity Radar's technical, community or
AI scoring stages and must not be represented as if it has.

A single opportunity, with the dimensions and reasons behind it.

The dimension breakdown is recomputed from the stored series rather than
read from the last snapshot, so it always describes the current state. That
it *can* be recomputed exactly is the engine's purity guarantee in use.

Thresholds and signals, verbatim.

Published for the same reason `/scores/model` and `/radar/categories` are:
a platform that warns you about something should be checkable on how it
decided to.

Radar entries whose supporting evidence is deteriorating.

Assessed live from the stored series rather than read from a cached verdict.
The engine is pure, so recomputing is exact — and a stale warning would be
worse than none.

Always unavailable, with the reason attached.

The endpoint exists rather than 404ing so that clients can render "not
collected" honestly and so the gap is discoverable in the API surface
instead of being an undocumented absence.

Highest peak return since detection.

Ranked by **peak**, not current: what the call was worth at its best is the
honest measure of the detection, and judging it by today's price would
credit or punish the platform for time it never claimed to predict.

schema.title: Response Get Hall Of Fame Api V1 Hall Of Fame Get

get.description:
Worst current return since detection.

This endpoint is the point of the whole record. Nothing is filtered, hidden
or softened: the entries here are detections that did not work, ranked by
how badly, and they are counted in exactly the same denominator as the Hall
of Fame. A platform that publishes only its winners has published nothing.

get.description:
Several boards in one response.

One request rather than six: the page shows them together, and six round
trips to render one screen is the pattern §8 already had to undo once.

able to tell "checked, nothing to compare" from "not checked".

get.description:
The brief, built only from stored events.

Scoped to the user's watched tokens by default. A brief covering 23,000
projects is a feed, and the whole purpose of this endpoint is to be short
enough to read.

schema.title: Response Brief Changes Api V1 Brief Changes Get

get.description: Unscoped and chronological — the operator's view, not the user's brief.

Opportunities that are live *right now*.

An empty board means nothing changed. That is information, not a fault, and
it must not be resolved by relaxing admission — `/health/pipeline` is where
a reader distinguishes "nothing happened" from "the pipeline stopped".

The live opportunity for a token, or a named past generation.

Addressing a past generation is what keeps the permanent record readable: a
closed call must stay retrievable after the same token opens a new one.

AppliedFilters.title: AppliedFilters
AppliedFilters.description:
Echo of what was actually applied.

Defaults that silently exclude rows are how a ranking endpoint returns 200
and an empty page with no explanation. Echoing them, alongside both counts,
makes the exclusion visible.

AuthResponse.title: AuthResponse
AuthResponse.description:
Login/register/refresh response.

The refresh token is deliberately absent: it is delivered as an httpOnly
cookie so browser JavaScript can never read it.

DimensionOut.title: DimensionOut
DimensionOut.description: One axis of the opportunity score.

reachable.title: Reachable
reachable.description: False when the model's available coverage cannot reach `min_evidence`. In v1 this is expected: the contract and holder signals do not exist yet.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: 0-100. Share of model weight that could be applied.

EvidenceSummary.title: EvidenceSummary
EvidenceSummary.description:
How much of the picture we have, and how recently we looked.

`evidence` is stored and time-invariant. `freshness` and `confidence` are
computed per request, so a stalled token reads as stale without anything
having to rewrite its row.

ExplanationOut.title: ExplanationOut
ExplanationOut.description:
Why this appeared *now*, in the five parts of AD-07.

Rendered from stored reason codes at read time. `limits` is not optional
padding — it is where the card says what could not be checked, which is the
difference between honest coverage and a card that quietly looks complete.

HallEntryOut.title: HallEntryOut
HallEntryOut.description:
One entry in the permanent record.

The same shape serves the Hall of Fame and the Hall of Lessons — they are
the same table ordered two ways, which is the point.

IdentityOut.title: IdentityOut
IdentityOut.description: Whether a token's name is contested, and where it sits in the queue.

captured_at.title: Captured At
captured_at.description: Last updated timestamp for this observation.

MetadataStatus.title: MetadataStatus
MetadataStatus.description:
Lifecycle of off-chain metadata resolution.

A token is recorded the moment it is detected, even when its metadata has
not been indexed yet — losing the discovery would be far worse than storing
a row whose name arrives a few seconds later.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: Declared share of the target vector.

available.title: Available
available.description: False for signals whose data source does not exist yet.

ModelComponentRead.title: ModelComponentRead
ModelComponentRead.description: One declared component of the active model.

available_weight_total.title: Available Weight Total
available_weight_total.description: Ceiling on coverage, and therefore on evidence, for this model.

ModelMetadataRead.title: ModelMetadataRead
ModelMetadataRead.description:
The active scoring model, exposed so its weights are inspectable.

The weights are priors, not fitted parameters. Publishing them is what makes
that claim checkable rather than asserted.

ModelOut.title: ModelOut
ModelOut.description: The published Radar model, so its claims are checkable.

OpportunityBoard.title: OpportunityBoard
OpportunityBoard.description:
The live board.

No `total`. An unconditional `count(*)` alongside the page is a measured
mistake — on `/scores/top` two of them cost 7.1 ms against a 0.4 ms ranking
query — and "how many exactly" is not a question anyone asks of a live
board. `has_more` answers the one that matters.

OpportunityOut.title: OpportunityOut
OpportunityOut.description: One card. One token, one generation, many live signals.

PerformanceOut.title: PerformanceOut
PerformanceOut.description:
The platform's track record.

Deliberately reports losers alongside winners. A success rate computed only
over the entries that worked is not a success rate.

RadarDetailOut.title: RadarDetailOut
RadarDetailOut.description: One opportunity in full, including why.

RadarDiscoveredCandidateOut.title: RadarDiscoveredCandidateOut
RadarDiscoveredCandidateOut.description: A Pump.fun admission candidate, before any intelligence scoring.

RadarEntryOut.title: RadarEntryOut
RadarEntryOut.description: A Radar opportunity, with everything measured from first detection.

has_veto.title: Has Veto
has_veto.description: True when the score was capped regardless of signals.

deduction.title: Deduction
deduction.description: Points removed from the opportunity score by the risk gate.

RiskSummary.title: RiskSummary
RiskSummary.description: What the risk gate took off, and whether it vetoed outright.

ScoreComponentRead.title: ScoreComponentRead
ScoreComponentRead.description:
One line of the score's waterfall.

Available contributions sum exactly to `opportunity_raw`; unavailable
components contribute nothing but keep their declared weight, which is what
makes a missing signal visible rather than quietly absent.

ScoreGrade.title: ScoreGrade
ScoreGrade.description:
Discrete band shown in the UI.

Bands exist so the product has a stable label to render: a score moving
68.2 → 69.1 should not look like news. Boundaries are a product decision
(design §21.1, open question 3), and adding a value later needs
`ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`, which is why they are settled before ship.

History is written on material change plus a periodic heartbeat, so this is

code.title: Code

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Which AI division owns this readout.

ScoreReasonRead.title: ScoreReasonRead
ScoreReasonRead.description:
One machine-readable reason plus the sentence it renders as.

The engine emits only codes; the template lives beside them and is applied
here. That keeps explanations translatable and diffable, and keeps prose out
of a path that runs tens of thousands of times an hour.

ScoreTrigger.title: ScoreTrigger
ScoreTrigger.description:
Why a history row was written.

Stored as a plain string column rather than a native enum, matching
`TokenEnrichmentState.tier`: these are diagnostic labels for a set expected
to grow, and a migration per added value is not worth the type safety here.

SignalOut.title: SignalOut
SignalOut.description: One live signal on an opportunity.

SmartMoneyBlock.title: SmartMoneyBlock
SmartMoneyBlock.description:
Wallet intelligence for one token.

Every figure is `None` rather than zero. "No smart wallets detected" and
"wallets cannot be seen" are different claims, and a zero would be read as
the first.
